method: Task-based development inspection using browser interaction, rendered screens, accessible markup and downloaded files
execution: Tool-operated development inspection; not observations from recruited participants or a record of individual teammates operating the app

checks.observation: Fresh draft showed zero ready fields, an invitation to enter an enquiry, and disabled approval.
Keyboard opened help; initial focus and Tab containment worked; Escape closed the dialog and returned focus to its opener.
A newly typed Harbour Table request produced restaurant, Sydney, 6 November 2026, 7 pm and four guests.
Opening Guests revealed the original customer message.
The correction changed four guests to six and retained restaurant, city and date. History showed the superseded value.
After 8 pm remained unresolved, approval was disabled, and the next question requested an exact time.
The staff offer of 8:30 pm did not resolve time before customer agreement.
Customer agreement resolved 8:30 pm and linked the offer and acceptance messages.
Editing the correction from six guests to five recalculated the count, retained 8:30 pm and removed approval.
A staff edit to seven stayed intact. A later thank-you exposed the existing five-versus-seven difference; revised text explains older support. Choosing Keep 7 restored approval eligibility.
Approval completed before editing. Native downloads delivered valid JSON and text containing six guests, 8:30 pm and reviewed status. Both state that no table is reserved.
The named device enquiry restored after refresh and reopened from the local library after starting a fresh draft.
An unresolved time triggered the draft warning; cancelling retained the draft.

A server started without OPENAI_API_KEY returned 503. The last valid brief and pending message remained. Retry was still reachable after dismissing the error and refreshing. Restoring normal configuration and choosing Retry completed the update.

Shortcut submission, help focus containment, Escape and focus return were observed. After the fix, Tab reached the import Cancel button with a visible 3px outline and Escape returned to Paste conversation.
At 390x844, conversation and brief switches, field editing and the core controls remained reachable. Document width was 390; no horizontal overflow was observed.
At 640x900, the inspected controls reflowed and document width was 640. This is not a native browser zoom test.

checks.environment: Production DOM inspection and computed styles
checks.observation: Selected controls had names and the page had a main landmark. Import aria-invalid, error/instruction references and dialog aria-describedby were added and verified in production. Selected opaque text/background pairs exceeded 4.5:1; screen-reader output was not tested.
Empty submission was disabled. An unlabelled 1001-character import displayed the speaker-label instruction and disabled Create booking brief. Cancel retained the existing draft.
Correct page title and meaningful content were observed; the captured production console log contained no warnings or errors in these states.

findings.finding: Existing disagreement with a staff edit was presented as a new change after an unrelated thank-you.
findings.fix: Show both values, explain older conversation support, and label the link View supporting message.
findings.verification: Local and deployed views showed revised copy; Keep 7 removed the review block.
findings.remainingLimit: A conversation that still differs from a staff edit may require another review after analysis.

findings.finding: Visible dialog instructions and import errors were not explicitly associated with their controls in accessibility markup.
findings.fix: Add aria-describedby, aria-invalid and labelled error/instruction references.
findings.verification: Production DOM linked dialog-description and import-feedback/import-replace-hint; invalid was true; import disabled.

limits: No evidence of satisfaction, learnability, workload or human time savings.
Checks cover the described tasks, not all product routes or all combinations.
Mobile and narrow-layout observations preceded the wording and accessibility-markup fixes; desktop retests verified those fixes.
Native zoom, screen-reader output and broader browser coverage were not tested.
Contrast calculations cover selected opaque text/background pairs, not full WCAG conformance.
Recovery fault was deliberately introduced locally; it is not a production outage statistic.
